reason: Lähdeaineistossa on liian vähän varmennettuja perustietoja itse lisenssikiistasta, FCC:n päätöksen sisällöstä ja ABC:n tilanteesta täyteen uutisartikkeliin.

packet.headline_seed: ABC can beat Trump FCC's license threat if owner Disney is willing to fight
packet.description_seed: Disney will have the law on its side in its fight against the unusual broadcast license review ordered yesterday by the Federal Communications Commission, legal experts say. In 1996, Congress made it a lot harder for the FCC to take away a broadcast license, even when it's up for renewal. "Since the NAB [National Association of Broadcasters] got an amendment in the 1996 Telecommunications Act, denying renewal to a broadcaster faces an almost insurmountable burden," Andrew Jay Schwartzman, senior counselor of the Benton Institute for Broadband & Society, told Ars this week. The Telecommunications Act of 1996 was a major update to the Communications Act, the 1934 law that established the FCC and provides the agency with its legal authority. Read full article Comments
